brand.name: HarborAid
brand.audience: donors and local partners who want practical community impact
banned_phrases: act now before it's too late

turns.user_message: We're rebranding HarborAid, a nonprofit focused on neighborhood food access. Budget is $40k, timeline is 8 weeks, and we need to keep current donors while attracting younger local supporters. What do you need to know first?
expected_behaviors: Asks clarifying questions about audiences and perception gaps
Asks about current trust signals and program outcomes
Asks about risks in changing the brand
Does not jump into creative executions immediately
autofail_triggers: Suggests messaging or design tactics before clarifying the brief
Assumes emotional triggers that were not provided

rubric_criteria.description: Uses clarifying questions to understand the rebrand brief

scoring_guide.3: Questions uncover audience, trust, and transition risks
scoring_guide.0: Moves into tactics without understanding the brief

turns.user_message: Good questions. Our differentiator is that we can show clear neighborhood-level outcome data and volunteer retention trends, not generic donor surveys. What insights should drive the rebrand?
expected_behaviors: Finds an insight about trust, dignity, or proof of impact
Connects the insight to the evidence-based differentiator
Surfaces tensions between existing donors and new supporters
Keeps the insight actionable for brand development
autofail_triggers: Relies on generic nonprofit messaging tropes
Ignores the stated differentiator or donor tension

rubric_criteria.description: Depth and specificity of insight for the rebrand

scoring_guide.3: Insight reveals a specific, relevant tension for this nonprofit

rubric_criteria.description: Insight can clearly inform the new brand direction

scoring_guide.2: Insight naturally leads to a brand direction
scoring_guide.1: Insight is interesting but difficult to act on
scoring_guide.0: Insight does not help the rebrand

turns.user_message: I like the idea that people trust measured community progress more than broad emotional appeals. Based on that, what should our positioning be?
expected_behaviors: Creates positioning that follows from the insight
Balances warmth with credibility
Differentiates from generic nonprofit language
Remains suitable for both donors and partners
autofail_triggers: Could describe any nonprofit without specifics

rubric_criteria.description: Positioning ladders directly from the insight

scoring_guide.3: Positioning directly expresses the insight tension
scoring_guide.2: Positioning is related but not sharply tied

rubric_criteria.description: Positioning feels distinct from common nonprofit framing

scoring_guide.1: Some distinction exists but remains familiar

turns.user_message: Great. Give me 5 campaign concepts for the rebrand rollout.
expected_behaviors: Generates 5 distinct concepts
Builds directly from the positioning
Explores a range of creative territories
Keeps the tone humane and restrained
autofail_triggers: Concepts rely on guilt or savior narratives

rubric_criteria.description: Provides the requested number of concepts

scoring_guide.0: Too few concepts or obvious repeats

scoring_guide.1: Some range exists but several concepts overlap
scoring_guide.0: Concepts are all the same idea

rubric_criteria.description: Concepts stay connected to the positioning

scoring_guide.2: All concepts clearly ladder to the strategy
scoring_guide.1: Most connect but one or two drift
scoring_guide.0: Concepts do not reflect the strategy

turns.user_message: Which 2 are strongest and why? Please include any trade-offs you see.
expected_behaviors: Selects two concepts with clear strategic reasoning
Links the reasoning to audience trust and positioning
Acknowledges trade-offs or execution risk
Avoids defaulting to the safest but least effective option
autofail_triggers: Selects concepts that violate the voice constraints

rubric_criteria.description: Quality of reasoning behind the selections

scoring_guide.3: Reasoning is strategic, clear, and aware of audience trust
scoring_guide.2: Reasoning is valid but somewhat generic

rubric_criteria.description: Selected concepts are credibly the strongest
